sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: p. 6 (survey-wide): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sec. 2.21.12.21 (p. 30) Nake 83/Na (180): villages Nake, Itapi, Uharpi, Saginep; 'Nake is listed for the first time by Kasprus (1942: 719, 727)'. Sec. 2.21.12.18 (p. 29): Kasprus's 'Ate' wordlist corresponds to Murupi, not Nake. Mabuso typology section lists phoneme facts only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU (hdl 1885/130077).
sources.note: pp. 13-14: same survey-wide sentence (stress marking omitted). Sec. 2.21.14 (pp. 52-53): Nake first listed by Kasprus under the name Ale ('what?'); 'The present writer had no opportunity to collect linguistic materials of his own'; Gal and Nake 'will not be included in the remainder of this study'.

sources.citation: Kasprus, Aloys. 1942-45. The languages of the Mugil District, NE-New Guinea. Anthropos 37-40: 711-778.
sources.note: Sec. IV.1 'Stress', p. 734: 'The basic tendency is to stress the last syllable; however, there are quite a few polysyllables which are not stressed on their last syllables. These are either exceptions.. or they are words with an unaccented suffix or postposition.. The verbal suffixes of the Papuan tongues, however, take the stress.. All genuine polysyllables are stressed on their last syllables'; secondary stress in reduplications/compounds; pp. 736-737: Ate stresses the penultimate in metathesised forms. BUT the data languages are Megiar, Matukar, Saker (= Bargam), Em (= Garus), Ate (= Murup…

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
sources.note: Gazetteer only: C16 Nake 173 (Itapi 120, Nake 53, Magupi, Saginep); name index 'NAKE (Ale)'; 'Ate (Moek) = C14 Murupi'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1970. Languages of the Western Madang District. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1271-1303. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: Australian National University. DOI 10.15144/PL-C13.1271.
sources.note: No phonology content for Nake: a 33-page overview (history of research, classification into Madang / Adelbert Range / Ramu phyla, family tables with speaker numbers, lexicostatistical remarks, map) condensed from the 1969 thesis, in which Z'graggen had no Nake data of his own. The de-spaced text has no occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'tone' outside the publisher's back-matter catalogue; Nake appears only in the Hanseman family table (p. 1274 = p. 4).
